judgements.reason: Universal covers is essentially finished in Tau Ceti (universal cover, pointed and unpointed Galois correspondence, π₁(S¹), π₁(RPⁿ), K(G,1) recognition all proved), whereas arithmetic Dirichlet series still lacks the final Wiener–Ikehara Tauberian step, the Dirichlet-density calculus and the prime-number-theorem transfer summit.

Both are largely built; arithmetic Dirichlet series still needs the last Wiener–Ikehara step, the density calculus and the PNT transfer, while spin representations still needs the Spin₄–Spin₆ isomorphisms, the L(ω) identification, triality including the order-three outer automorphism of Spin₈, and Kostant's isotypy corollary for semisimple Lie algebras, a somewhat larger and deeper remainder.

Spin representations has a large built base with a few summits left (Spin₄–Spin₆, L(ω), triality, Kostant isotypy), whereas p-adic measures must build measures on profinite spaces, completed group rings, Mahler–Amice theory, Λ-module structure and characteristic ideals, determinant lines and Gorenstein duality with only Mathlib's Mahler basis and Weierstrass preparation to start from, plus rigid weight spaces that need unbuilt rigid geometry.

CFSG already has carriers for 13 of 17 Lie-type constructors and all 26 sporadic presentations, leaving the ³D₄, Ree and Tits carriers, the final assembly and the L5 Chevalley–Demazure agreement; p-adic measures needs seven stacked unbuilt layers (measures, completed group rings, Mahler–Amice, Λ-modules, determinants, Gorenstein duality) plus rigid geometry for its weight spaces.

CFSG's remainder is three explicit carrier families, the uniform assembly and L5 (uniform Chevalley–Demazure schemes and agreement), while PDE still lacks Calderón–Zygmund theory, interpolation and BMO, trace, extension, Morrey and Hölder spaces, Green/Poisson/Perron potential theory, Schauder, W^{2,p} and De Giorgi–Nash–Moser regularity, and parabolic Galerkin theory.

PDE's missing lanes (harmonic analysis, boundary Sobolev theory, potential theory, elliptic regularity, parabolic existence) are voluminous but sit about three layers deep on Mathlib's analysis; Shimura data needs comparable volume stacked on unbuilt imports (Weil restriction, adelic points, flag schemes, real Lie groups with van Est) and on missing real-reductive structure for Cartan involutions, Hermitian symmetric domains, variations of Hodge structure and reflex-field descent.

Pro-p groups has its Sylow, Frattini and Burnside base built and needs free pro-p groups, the H² dictionary, cd theory, Demushkin duality and Labute's classification over existing profinite and low-degree cohomology foundations; Shimura data needs a similar amount but on absent foundations: Weil restriction, adelic points, flag schemes, real Lie groups and Cartan involutions, Hermitian domains, VHS and reflex fields.

Pro-p groups needs free pro-p groups, extensions and H², cd theory, Demushkin duality and Labute's classification over non-arithmetic profinite cohomology; quadratic form invariants needs Witt rings, Brauer and Clifford invariants, the dyadic Hilbert symbol and local classification, crossed products for Br ≅ H² and Kahn's formula, and also imports unbuilt local-field arithmetic, Hilbert 90, Kummer theory and the Evens norm for G_K, plus class field theory for its bridges.

Quadratic form invariants' main targets need Witt and Brauer invariants, the local Hilbert-symbol classification, crossed products for Br ≅ H², Stiefel–Whitney classes and Kahn's formula plus imported local-field and Galois-cohomology pieces (class field theory only for comparison bridges); DGA must build DG and A∞ categories with modules and bimodules, transfer, bar–cobar, twisted complexes and Perf, derived Morita theory, DG quotients, Hochschild deformation theory, CY completions with HRR and Koszul duality, a larger stack with only the DG/A∞ algebra definitions in place.

DGA's missing layers are voluminous but rest on Mathlib's homological and triangulated foundations; the Jacobian challenge needs coherent-cohomology finiteness and Serre duality for schemes, cohomology and base change, Symᵈ X, fppf descent, representability and properness of Pic⁰, dual abelian varieties and polarizations, and the Albanese property, deeper foundational algebraic geometry that is almost entirely absent.

The Jacobian challenge is large but self-contained algebraic geometry; automorphic spectral theory needs Eisenstein series with meromorphic continuation, Arthur truncation, the full spectral decomposition and the invariant trace formula on top of 20 unbuilt imported stages (adelic reduction theory, automorphic forms on reductive groups, smooth local representations with second adjointness).

Gross–Zagier imports automorphic spectral theory through AS.4 together with many further unbuilt roadmaps (Arakelov heights, Shimura curves, Jacquet–Langlands, theta correspondence, Heegner points, p-adic Hodge regulators, the Jacobian challenge), then stacks Waldspurger, arithmetic generating series and the YZZ formula on top.

K-theory of finite and local fields needs higher algebraic K-theory, spectra, THH/TC, de Rham–Witt and étale K-theory (about 104 largely unbuilt upstream stages, chain depth about 24), but Gross–Zagier's import tree is several times larger (about 460 largely unbuilt stages across 72 roadmaps, depth about 92), containing automorphic spectral theory, Shimura curves, Arakelov geometry and p-adic Hodge theory.

Universal covers has every stage proved in Tau Ceti, while spin representations still lacks the Spin₄–Spin₆ isomorphisms, the highest-weight identification of the spin modules, triality and Kostant's isotypy corollary.

DGA is a large but self-contained algebraic theory on Mathlib's homological foundations; K-theory of local fields must first import unbuilt higher algebraic K-theory (plus and Q-constructions), stable homotopy theory, topological K-theory, THH/TC with the cyclotomic trace, de Rham–Witt complexes and étale K-theory before Quillen's and Hesselholt–Madsen's calculations.

Arithmetic Dirichlet series is nearly complete (Wiener–Ikehara's last step, density calculus, PNT transfer), whereas Shimura data has nothing at datum level and needs Weil restriction, adelic points, flag schemes, real Lie groups, Hermitian symmetric domains, variations of Hodge structure and reflex fields.

CFSG lacks only three carrier families, the uniform assembly and the L5 agreement with Chevalley–Demazure schemes; quadratic form invariants lacks nearly everything above basic Witt theory (Witt ring, Brauer and Clifford invariants, local Hilbert symbol and classification, Br ≅ H² via crossed products, Stiefel–Whitney classes, Kahn's formula) and its local-field and Galois-cohomology imports.

Both need a large amount; PDE's missing lanes sit about three layers deep on Mathlib's analysis, while p-adic measures stacks seven unbuilt layers from measures and completed group rings through Λ-module structure, determinant lines and Gorenstein duality, and its weight spaces need rigid geometry and locally analytic distributions that are not in the library.

The Jacobian challenge needs coherent cohomology, base change, the Picard functor and abelian-variety duality; K-theory of local fields needs the far larger stack of higher algebraic K-theory, spectra, topological Hochschild and cyclic homology, de Rham–Witt complexes and étale K-theory comparisons.

Pro-p groups sits on a built profinite, Sylow and Frattini base and needs free pro-p groups, cd theory and Demushkin theory; automorphic spectral theory needs Eisenstein series, truncation, the spectral decomposition and the trace formula over 20 unbuilt imported stages on adelic groups, automorphic forms and local representations.

DGA is a self-contained homological theory, whereas Gross–Zagier imports about 460 largely unbuilt stages (automorphic spectral theory, Shimura curves, Arakelov intersection theory, Jacobians, theta correspondence, p-adic Hodge theory) before its own height and period layers.

Arithmetic Dirichlet series is mostly built with a small analytic remainder, whereas p-adic measures and Iwasawa algebras is essentially unbuilt: measures, completed group rings, Mahler–Amice theory, Λ-modules and characteristic ideals, determinant lines, Gorenstein duality and rigid weight spaces.

The amounts are comparable: PDE lacks harmonic analysis, boundary Sobolev theory, potential theory, elliptic regularity and parabolic existence at depth about three, while quadratic form invariants lacks Witt rings, Brauer invariants, the dyadic local classification, crossed products and Kahn's formula stacked on unbuilt imports (local-field ramification, Hilbert 90, Kummer and Evens norm for G_K, class field theory for its bridges), which makes it deeper.

Spin representations has only a few remaining summits (Spin₄–Spin₆, L(ω), triality, Kostant isotypy), while Shimura data needs Weil restriction, adelic points, flag schemes, real Lie groups with Cartan involutions, Hermitian symmetric domains, VHS, compact duals and reflex fields, none of which is in the library.
